description: The Erlang virtual machine: millions of lightweight processes with no shared memory, each with its own heap and garbage collector, watched by supervisors.
A partition key of channel plus a fixed time window, so one channel's history is split into partitions of bounded size.
One partition receiving a large share of the traffic; the nodes that hold it slow down every query they serve.
ScyllaDB's design: each CPU core owns a slice of the data with its own cache, MemTables and SSTables, avoiding cross-core locking.
Concurrent requests for the same row share one in-flight database query; later callers subscribe to its result.
Time a runtime stops or slows application work to reclaim memory; a node-wide pause stalls every request on that node.
The latency that 99% of requests beat; it exposes pauses and hot spots that an average hides.
